pr_title: Check all search filter attributes are filterable upfront
pr_body:
# Pull Request

## Related issue
Fixes #5069

## What does this PR do?
- checks all `fid`s in the `Filter` tree are filterable before evaluating search query
- returns AttributeNotFilterable error if any are not

## PR checklist
Please check if your PR fulfills the following requirements:
- [x] Does this PR fix an existing issue, or have you listed the changes applied in the PR description (and why they are needed)?
- [x] Have you read the contributing guidelines?
- [x] Have you made sure that the title is accurate and descriptive of the changes?

Thank you so much for contributing to Meilisearch!

issue_context.title: Filter error ignored on search request
issue_context.body:
**Describe the bug**
When searching using `POST /indexes/{indexUid}/search` there is a strange behavior when there is an error coming from the `filter` param. Depending on the `filter` object, sometimes, even if an error is present, Meilisearch just returns no documents without any error. It happens when adding more filter items in an array (creating AND), but does not seem linked to the number of filter items in the array, rather maybe the length of each independent filter item maybe.

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Index the movies dataset
2. Add `genres` as filterable

Try with these requests
```
req: POST /indexes/movies/search
params: {
  "facets": [
    "genres"
  ],
  "filter": [
    "test=test"
  ],
  "limit": 20
}
error: {
  "message": "Attribute `test` is not filterable. Available filterable attributes are: `genres`.\n1:5 test=test",
  "code": "invalid_search_filter",
  "type": "invalid_request",
  "link": "https://docs.meilisearch.com/errors#invalid_search_filter"
}
```
🔝 This is expected ✅ 
```
req: POST /indexes/movies/search
params: {
  "facets": [
    "genres"
  ],
  "filter": [
    "genres=\"Action\"",
    "test=test"
  ],
  "limit": 20
}
response: {
  "message": "Attribute `test` is not filterable. Available filterable attributes are: `genres`.\n1:5 test=test",
  "code": "invalid_search_filter",
  "type": "invalid_request",
  "link": "https://docs.meilisearch.com/errors#invalid_search_filter"
}
```
🔝 This is expected ✅ 

```
req: POST /indexes/movies/search
params: {
  "facets": [
    "genres"
  ],
  "filter": [
    "genres=\"Action\"",
    "genres=\"Adventure\"",
    "genres=\"Animation\"",
    "genres=\"Comedy\"",
    "test=test"
  ],
  "limit": 20
}
response: {
    "hits": [],
    "query": "",
    "processingTimeMs": 0,
    "limit": 20,
    "offset": 0,
    "estimatedTotalHits": 0,
    "facetDistribution": {
        "genres": {}
    },
    "facetStats": {}
}
```
🔝 This is not expected and the response should be the same as previous examples 🔴
 
**Expected behavior**
Meilisearch should respond an `error` if a `filter` is wrong, in all cases.

**Meilisearch version:**
v1.11.3

**Additional context**
Tested with the Meilisearch Cloud search preview
comments: It looks like it returns the 0 hits response if one of the earlier filter conditions matches nothing (e.g. `"genres=\"nomatch\"`), so it never reaches the `"test=test"` condition

review_comments: `fids()` is doing extra traversal of the `Filter` tree every search, so wasn't sure about this approach. Better might be to gather attributes to be checked during `Filter` construction (in [`Filter::from_str`](https://github.com/meilisearch/meilisearch/blob/b21d7aedf9096539041362d438e973a18170f3fc/crates/milli/src/search/facet/filter.rs#L210)), though it looked like it could involve a lot of refactoring
